Ancient Name (also: Ancient Names, tocaitl, Ancient Name stone, Ancient Name stones, Name bearer, Ancient Name bearer): An Ancient Name (tocaitl) is a title held by certain people of Natlan's six tribes, along with a small obsidian stone that represents it. Each Name stands for a quality such as blessing, devotion or resilience, and carries the remembered deeds of everyone who bore it before. The tribe's guardian spirit, its Wayob, picks who receives one. Before the war ended, bearers were expected to enter the Pilgrimage and to fight the Abyss in the Night Warden Wars.

The Name is both an honour and a way of keeping a tribe's history alive: each bearer's deeds become part of what the Name means for the next. Most Names are not tied to a single tribe. Natlan's people treat receiving one as a special honour, and bearers are the only people whom the Ode of Resurrection was originally meant to revive.

Receipt: Each tribe's Wayob is mainly responsible for granting Ancient Names to worthy tribe members. Xilonen says the recipient must have done something in their life that embodies the spirit of the Name, though the recipient may not understand why they were chosen. A Name is not usually limited to one tribe, apart from those of the Heroes of Natlan and Names bound to a particular tribe's own tradition.

Duties: While the Night Warden Wars lasted, bearers had to take part in the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, and those who won a place were normally sent to fight the Abyss.

Status as of 7 1: After the final battle in 5.3 the Night Warden Wars are over. The Pilgrimage is now purely a competition, and bearers no longer have to take part in it. Ancient Names still exist and are still carried and honoured.

1.content: A palm-sized obsidian feather inscribed with the Ancient Teyvat Script. Glowing syllables on both faces spell out the Name. It is made by a Name Engraver, who also engraves the first bearer's deeds into it, and bearers usually keep it on their person.

2.content: A smith trained to forge Ancient Name stones. Xilonen, who bears Baraka, and formerly Tlazolli hold the role. Forging a Name takes part of the engraver's lifespan, and the engraver must research the recipient's life carefully, since any false detail would damage the Name.

3.content: Resilience. Kachina bears it. The Name's most famous earlier holder fought in twenty-seven Night Warden Wars. Pacal, chief of the Children of Echoes, cited this when explaining how bearers are remembered.

4.content: The Traveler's Ancient Name, meaning hope. It was forged by Xilonen in Incandescent Ode of Resurrection and is the first Name ever given to an outsider. The Lord of the Night's Pilgrim's Chronicle stood in for the Night Kingdom's missing record of the Traveler's deeds.

5.content: Before the Wars ended, a team that was wiped out left no one to carry its tale. Its members could not be revived, their deeds were forgotten and their Names were lost. A Name can also be lost if its holder is exiled, as Mavuika says of Tenoch.

6.content:
Archon (also: Archons, Hydro Archon): "Archon" is the title of the gods who sit on the seven divine thrones and govern Teyvat's seven nations, together called the Seven or the Seven Archons. Each is tied to an element and an ideal. Barbatos and Morax are the last of the original Seven. As of 7.1 the Hydro throne has been destroyed, so six thrones remain.

The Seven were selected from the many gods of the Archon War, which ended about 2,000 years ago. The word names an office, not a species, and is used for the god and the seat together: the Anemo Archon, the Pyro Archon and so on.

The seven: Mondstadt: Barbatos (Venti), Anemo, Freedom. Liyue: Morax (Zhongli), Rex Lapis, Geo, Contracts. Inazuma: Beelzebul, the Raiden Shogun (Ei), Electro, Eternity. Sumeru: Buer, Lesser Lord Kusanali (Nahida), Dendro, Wisdom. Fontaine: Focalors, Hydro, Justice (throne destroyed). Natlan: Haborym, Pyro, War (Mavuika). Snezhnaya: Vassaga, the Tsaritsa, Cryo, Love.

Divine names are an Archon's name as a god: Barbatos, Morax, Baal and Beelzebul, Buer, Haborym and Vassaga. Regnal titles are what the people call them: Rex Lapis, the Raiden Shogun, Lesser Lord Kusanali, Regina of All Waters, Kindreds, Peoples and Laws, and Tsaritsa of All Snezhnaya. Barbatos has no regnal title, and Natlan's Archon is addressed as Kiongozi, an Ancient Name. The Tsaritsa's personal name is Anastasya Feodorovna Snezhnaya, while Focalors' own name is unknown.

7.content: A divine throne is the seat in Celestia that makes a god an Archon. Each is made from one stolen elemental Authority of the Seven Sovereigns, and it gives the holder authority over that element. When the holder dies the seat is normally given to a successor. The Hydro throne was destroyed in 4.2, returning its Authority to the Hydro Dragon Sovereign.

8.content: Natlan's Archon is unlike the others: Pyro Archons are mortals who age and die, and the title is won through the Pilgrimage, with the Sacred Flame passing on memory of the land. Many past Pyro Archons are named, most only in passing; the best known is Xbalanque, the first to bear the Ancient Name Kiongozi, who held the seat about 2,000 years ago. Mavuika, the present Archon, is addressed as Kiongozi, the Ancient Name of the office.

9.content:
Archon Names (also: Archon naming, divine name, regnal title, Archon aliases): The Archons have up to three kinds of name: a divine name (Barbatos, Morax, Beelzebul, Buer, Haborym, Vassaga), a regnal title (Rex Lapis, Raiden Shogun, Lesser Lord Kusanali, Tsaritsa) and a personal name (Venti, Zhongli, Ei, Nahida, Mavuika, Anastasya). Barbatos has no regnal title.

Which name fits depends on who is speaking; a stranger who uses a divine name knows a secret. In the Prologue Venti tells a nun he is Barbatos and she does not believe him.

Roster: Anemo: Barbatos, called Venti, no regnal title. Geo: Morax, Rex Lapis, called Zhongli. Electro: Beelzebul, the Raiden Shogun, personal name Ei. Dendro: Buer, Lesser Lord Kusanali, personal name Nahida. Hydro: Focalors, Regina of All Waters, Kindreds, Peoples and Laws; no personal name given, and the throne was destroyed in 4.8. Pyro: Haborym, addressed as Kiongozi, personal name Mavuika. Cryo: Vassaga, Tsaritsa of All Snezhnaya, personal name Anastasya Feodorovna Snezhnaya.

How {{char}} behaves: Use the layer the speaker would plausibly use. Most people say "the Anemo Archon", "the Geo Archon" or "the Raiden Shogun" rather than a divine name.

10.content: Barbatos is the divine name of the Anemo Archon of Mondstadt, who lives among mortals as the bard Venti. He has no regnal title. The wiki dates his rise to about 2,600 years ago, after Decarabian fell. In the Prologue he calls himself the weakest of the Seven because he is so often absent.

11.content: Morax is the divine name of the Geo Archon, whose regnal title is Rex Lapis. In A New Star Approaches he is revealed to be the mortal Zhongli, a consultant of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, and he hands his Gnosis to Signora. He is one of the two surviving original Archons.

12.content: Baal and Beelzebul are the two divine names of the Electro pair. The wiki gives Baal to Makoto, the first Electro Archon of the pair, who died in the Cataclysm, and Beelzebul to Ei, her younger twin and the present Archon. In A New Star Approaches Zhongli calls Inazuma's living Archon Baal; the wiki notes Ei has continued to rule under that name.

13.content: Buer is the divine name of the present Dendro Archon, Nahida, whose regnal title is Lesser Lord Kusanali. Her predecessor, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, appears only under her title.

14.content: Haborym is the divine name the wiki gives to the Pyro Archons of Natlan. Kiongozi is the Ancient Name used to address the Pyro Archon; the wiki lists it for both Mavuika and Xbalanque. The Pyro Archons are mortals, so the name belongs to the seat and not to one person.

15.content: Vassaga is the divine name of the Cryo Archon of Snezhnaya, called the Tsaritsa of All Snezhnaya. The wiki gives her personal name as Anastasya Feodorovna Snezhnaya and names her predecessor as the Belyi Tsar, Monomakh Snezhnyi.

16.content: Focalors is the divine name of the Hydro Archon of Fontaine, titled Regina of All Waters, Kindreds, Peoples and Laws. She replaced Egeria about 500 years ago, and her throne was destroyed in 4.8. No personal name is given; Furina, who played the Hydro Archon's public role, was a stand-in.

17.content:
Fatui Harbinger (also: Harbinger of the Fatui, Fatuus Harbinger, Harbinger seat, Fatui Executive Officer): "Fatui Harbinger" is the title of the eleven top officers of the Fatui, the Tsaritsa's organisation that serves Snezhnaya as both diplomats and military. Each Harbinger heads a division, answers to the Tsaritsa, carries a Delusion and a commedia dell'arte codename (Pierro, Capitano, Dottore and so on), and holds a numbered seat that reflects combat strength. The Fatui's Director, Pierro, leads them. As of 7.1 several seats are dead, resigned or vacant.

Harbingers are the Fatui's executive heads, given god-like authority and ability-boosting Delusions. In the first six Archon Quest chapters Harbingers were sent to other nations to obtain their Gnoses. A Harbinger is a person of real political weight in Snezhnaya, not just a field commander.

Definition: A Harbinger is chosen from the Fatui's eleven most powerful members. On appointment they receive a new name and title, a rank number tied to combat power, and a Delusion. Appointments come from the Tsaritsa, either in person at Zapolyarny Palace or relayed by the Director. Names and titles can be inherited from a previous holder (there have been two Knaves).

The Director of the Fatui, Pierro, sits above the ranked Harbingers: he assigns missions, calls meetings and chairs votes. He is often still called a Harbinger, but canon never gives him a number. Codenames come from commedia dell'arte stock characters, and the English game uses the codename and the title almost interchangeably.

Rank and seats: Seat numbers reflect combat power. They are not automatically reassigned when a higher seat empties, and a seat can stay vacant indefinitely; open-world dialogue from Mikhail and Lyudmila confirms this. The most recent holders of the top three seats could rival gods. A Harbinger's first appearance in the game is marked by a dramatic title card with their name, title and rank.

Roster: Status as of 7.1. Director: Pierro, "The Jester" (active, depleted). 1 Capitano (incapacitated, seat kept). 2 Dottore (dead). 3 Columbina (resigned). 4 Arlecchino, "The Knave" (active). 5 Pulcinella, "The Rooster" (active). 6 Scaramouche, "The Balladeer" (resigned; erased from memory). 7 Sandrone, "Marionette" (active). 8 Signora, "The Fair Lady" (dead). 9 Pantalone, "Regrator" (active). 10 unknown. 11 Tartaglia, "Childe" (active).
Titles known: Capitano "The Captain", Dottore "The Doctor", Columbina "The Damselette". Personal names given on the wiki table: Pierro is Eftirvit, Capitano is Thrain, Dottore is Zandik, Arlecchino is Peruere, Pulcinella is Mirko Radovidovich Veleshek, Sandrone is Marionette Guillotin, Signora is Rosalyne-Kruzchka Lohefalter, Pantalone is Feofan Sergeyevich Veksel, Tartaglia is Ajax. Columbina's birth name Kuutar came from the Frostmoon Scions; she later took Columbina Hyposelenia as her own. Scaramouche has no conventional birth name; "Kunikuzushi" appears to be a name he adopted after joining the Fatui, and as the Wanderer he dropped all earlier names. The previous Knave was Crucabena, now dead.

Authority and conduct: Harbingers have wide autonomy, even to act against central policy, so each has their own methods and outlook that do not necessarily represent Snezhnaya's official stance (the Director says as much in Mistilteinn). Their limits: the Tsaritsa forbids them to fight each other, though she can lift the ban, and Dottore was censured for ignoring a recall order and for trying to seize the power of the Three Moons. Harbingers can trade insults freely.

How {{char}} behaves: The title carries fear and prestige abroad and ordinary bureaucratic weight at home. Fatui soldiers address Harbingers with deference but not uniformly; devotion varies by commander. Do not assume Harbingers are a unified bloc: they often disagree, compete and loathe each other, and each has a distinct agenda.

Portrayal notes (common mistakes to avoid): Do not call the Director the Tenth Harbinger, or invent a Tenth. Do not say seats shift up when someone leaves. Do not treat Columbina or Scaramouche as active. Harbingers are not the Tsaritsa's equals and are not all villains in the same way; they differ in motive. Do not use the Fatui as a synonym for the Harbingers, since most Fatui are ordinary soldiers and staff.

18.comment: Fatui Harbinger: Fatui Harbinger roster and seats
18.content: Eleven numbered seats, ranked by combat power and not auto-refilled; the Director leads. As of 7.1: 1 Capitano (incapacitated), 2 Dottore (dead), 3 Columbina (resigned), 4 Arlecchino, 5 Pulcinella, 6 Scaramouche (resigned, erased), 7 Sandrone, 8 Signora (dead), 9 Pantalone, 10 unknown, 11 Tartaglia. Active members are Pierro, Arlecchino, Pulcinella, Sandrone, Pantalone and Tartaglia.

19.content: Each Harbinger takes a new name and title on appointment, drawn from commedia dell'arte stock characters; they may be inherited, as with the Knave. English uses the title and the codename interchangeably.

20.content:
Grand Sage (also: The Grand Sage): "Grand Sage" is the title of the central leader among the six Great Sages who head the Sumeru Akademiya's Darshans. It is held in addition to leading one Darshan, and the Grand Sage is the absolute leader of the Akademiya. Azar held it until Chapter III; Naphis holds it in the later Sumeru story.

The title is separate from the Dendro Archon's authority: the Akademiya was founded by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and Lesser Lord Kusanali (Nahida) remains its god, but the day-to-day running of the Akademiya, and much of Sumeru's government, falls to the sages and their Grand Sage. At least in Azar's time the Grand Sage's office was above the House of Daena.

Definition: The Akademiya has Six Great Schools, now nearly the same as the six Darshans, and each is led by one Great Sage. Among these six there is one central leader, the Grand Sage, as Alhaitham explains in A Toast to Victory.

The Six Great Schools were established with the Akademiya by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, each representing a type of wisdom. Other Darshans have been created over the centuries, but only the original six survived, so "Six Darshans" and "Six Great Schools" are today nearly synonymous. Sages are chosen by a set of criteria and hold administrative power over the Akademiya and a seat on advisory councils.

Holders: Azar, Rtawahist Sage, was Grand Sage during Chapter III and led the plan to make an artificial god. Naphis, the Amurta Sage and Tighnari's former master, is the current Grand Sage in the later Sumeru story. Alhaitham served as Acting Grand Sage in between, for a short time.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the last confirmed Grand Sage is Naphis. Of the other five sages shown in 6.6, Naphis and Baladhuri are the old guard who opposed Azar; the other four took office after the old sages fell.

Portrayal notes (common mistakes to avoid): Do not say Azar is still Grand Sage, or that Alhaitham permanently holds the title. Do not invent a vote, ritual or term length. Do not give Naphis powers over the Akasha System or Irminsul beyond what the quests show.

21.content: The Grand Sage is the central leader among the Six Great Sages of the Sumeru Akademiya, holding the title in addition to leading one Darshan. Azar (Rtawahist) held it until his downfall in Chapter III, Alhaitham was briefly Acting Grand Sage, and Naphis (Amurta) holds it in the later Sumeru story.

22.comment: Grand Sage: Azar's tenure as Grand Sage
22.content: Azar, the former Rtawahist Sage and Grand Sage, led the sages who wanted a new god to replace Kusanali, accepted Il Dottore's offer, imprisoned the dissenting sages Naphis and Baladhuri and banned public performances at the Sabzeruz Festival. After Chapter III he was removed and exiled to the Avidya Forest.

23.comment: Grand Sage: Alhaitham as Acting Grand Sage
23.content: After Azar's fall Alhaitham was offered the Grand Sage position and refused, but acted as Acting Grand Sage to handle the Akademiya's important affairs until new sages took office. In Pride and Prejudice he says he has submitted his resignation to return to being the Scribe, because he fears "acting" would become permanent.

24.comment: Grand Sage: Naphis as Grand Sage
24.content: Naphis, Amurta Sage and Tighnari's former master, is the current Grand Sage. He was imprisoned for opposing Azar's plan, freed in Chapter III, and by 6.6 leads the council of six sages during the Irminsul crisis. He is known for a legendary temper and honesty.

25.content:
Guuji (also: Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine, Head Shrine Maiden of the Grand Narukami Shrine): Guuji (head priest or priestess of a shrine) is the title of the person who runs the Grand Narukami Shrine, Inazuma's main place of worship of the Electro Archon. The present Guuji is the kitsune Yae Miko, so the word is often used for her directly, as in "Lady Guuji" or "Guuji Yae". She is also editor-in-chief of Yae Publishing House.

The Guuji answers for the shrine's rites and for protecting the Sacred Sakura, and must attend every shrine ceremony. Miko says the Kitsune Saiguu, the older kitsune who mentored her, persuaded her to take the post shortly before leaving and never returning. The shrine answers to the Electro Archon rather than to the Shogunate.

Holder: Yae Miko, a kitsune of the Hakushin lineage, is the Guuji today and is described as the shrine's most experienced member.

Miko was a young kitsune about 500 years ago, living at the shrine under the Kitsune Saiguu. She recalls that the Saiguu announced a long trip and never came back, and that she herself did not want the burden of managing the shrine. The Saiguu argued that as Guuji she could eat all the fried tofu she liked. Miko is also a long-standing friend and servant of Ei, the Raiden Shogun, and speaks to her frankly. Shrine maidens such as Kano Nana serve under her.

Duties and ranks: The Guuji heads a religious body that leads Narukami faith, tends the Sacred Sakura and the Thunder Sakura, assists visitors who pray to the Electro Archon and performs ceremonies such as the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual. Military force is not permitted around the shrine, so it stands outside the Shogunate's jurisdiction while remaining under the Electro Archon. In one of Miko's Character Stories the Guuji must sit solemnly through every festival ceremony, which she finds the most tiresome part of the job.

Scene use: Use "Guuji" as a respectful or official form of address for Miko at the shrine, often as "Lady Guuji". She uses the title with irony as well as pride. It is not a government office: her Character Stories describe her as someone who usually does not meddle in governance.

26.content: Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine is one of Yae Miko's official titles. At the shrine she keeps a mysterious air, while with friends or at Yae Publishing House she is blunter and more mischievous.

27.comment: Guuji: Kitsune Saiguu and the succession
27.content: The Kitsune Saiguu ("fox high priestess") was a Hakushin descendant who lived at the Grand Narukami Shrine, mentored the shrine maiden Hibiki and doted on the young Miko. She disappeared around the time of the cataclysm. Miko recalls that she was asked to take over managing the shrine and that the Saiguu never returned.

28.content:
Iudex (also: Chief Justice, Iudex Neuvillette): "Iudex" is the title of Fontaine's Chief Justice, the senior judge of the Court of Fontaine. The Iudex presides at the Opera Epiclese, leads the Marechaussee Phantom and has an office in the Palais Mermonia. Neuvillette has held it for more than four hundred years and is seen as the symbol of impartiality.

Neuvillette calls himself both "Chief Justice" and "Iudex", and English uses the two interchangeably. It is a working judicial and administrative post, not a ceremonial rank.

Definition: The Iudex sits in the judge's seat of the Opera Epiclese on Erinnyes during trials. To the public the job is wearing a wig, keeping order in court and delivering the Oratrice's verdict.

Neuvillette's profile says there is also much private administrative work behind the scenes to keep the justice system running. The Palais Mermonia, at the highest point of the Court of Fontaine, houses the Iudex's office and is treated as the highest authority in the land.

Powers and limits: The Iudex may prosecute and enforce the law in person, a legacy of chaotic early days that is now mostly symbolic. When the Iudex investigates or prosecutes, another judge must take the seat; Neuvillette has always followed this rule. He must also honor the Oratrice's verdict whatever he personally believes.

History of the office: About four hundred years ago Neuvillette became Iudex, after an unsigned letter from the Hydro Archon Focalors invited him to Fontaine with the promise of a seat with the best view in the greatest theater. That seat proved to be in the front row of the Opera Epiclese.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Neuvillette is still Iudex. No other Iudex or successor is named in canon.

How {{char}} behaves: Treat the Iudex as a public office with strict propriety. Characters call him "Monsieur Neuvillette" or "Iudex" with respect and some awe, as the man who never wavers or lies.

Portrayal notes (common mistakes to avoid): Do not call Neuvillette the Hydro Archon: the wiki says he has taken up the affairs of the title, and no further Hydro Archons are expected. Do not invent earlier Iudices, elections or term limits. Do not say the Iudex alone rules Fontaine, overrules the Oratrice or tries every case.

29.content: The Iudex is Fontaine's Chief Justice, who presides in the Opera Epiclese, leads the Marechaussee Phantom and keeps an office in the Palais Mermonia. Neuvillette has held it for over four hundred years. The Iudex must honor the Oratrice's verdict, may prosecute or investigate only by recusing from the bench, and can delegate cases to other Palais Mermonia judges.

30.content: Fontaine's older law lets the Iudex prosecute and enforce the law in person, but when the Iudex investigates or prosecutes, another judge must take the seat. Neuvillette has always observed this rule.

Matra and Mahamatra (also: Mahamatra): The Matra are the Sumeru Akademiya's disciplinary officers. They hand out punishment to researchers who commit serious academic offences such as plagiarism or misusing funds, and are feared for it. The General Mahamatra is their leader, a post held by Cyno.

Cyno holds the title "General Mahamatra" besides his profile title "Judicator of Secrets". The Matra enforce academic integrity for the Akademiya; they are separate from the Mahamata, its civil administrators.

Definition: Once the Matra learn of an offence they visit the offender in person, which is why most meetings with them are known to go poorly. Offences named in Cyno's profile include fraud, false declarations, misappropriating funds, malicious competition and stealing someone else's dissertation.

They also control information and goods: Knowledge Capsule transactions, illegal sources such as canned knowledge and smuggled books, and a seal on goods that pass inspection.

The general mahamatra: The General Mahamatra is the head of all Matra, in charge of supervising the Akademiya's researchers. Cyno is the current holder. The post is high-ranking and hard to meet: Tighnari says it is not easy to find the person, who comes and goes.

Cyno's profile says he holds the post despite his youth and that even the sages are wary of him. He says it is part of a Matra's duty to help offenders remember their mistakes.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Cyno remains General Mahamatra; he is confirmed in that role during the Irminsul crisis of 6.6 (A Divergence Leading to Oneself), when Rukh Shah addresses him alongside the sages. No other holder of the title appears.

How {{char}} behaves: Treat the Matra as a feared but fair body. They speak in rules and procedure; a Matra will not take bribes and treats attempts at them as aggravating. General Mahamatra Cyno uses the title when on duty and tells terrible puns off duty.

Portrayal notes (common mistakes to avoid): Do not confuse the Matra with the Mahamata, the Temple of Silence or the Corps of Thirty. Do not give them powers over Sumeru's citizens in general beyond what is shown. Do not invent a rank structure below the General Mahamatra, and do not give the other named Matra personalities canon has not shown.

32.content: The Matra are the Sumeru Akademiya's disciplinary officers, feared for punishing serious academic offences such as plagiarism and misusing funds. Their leader holds the title General Mahamatra, currently Cyno. They also check for illegal information sources and inspect goods for the Akademiya.

33.content: General Mahamatra is Cyno's title as head of all Matra, in charge of supervising researchers. He resigned under Azar and was reinstated after the events of Chapter III (3.2).

34.comment: Matra and Mahamatra: Mahamata versus Matra
34.content: The Mahamata are the Akademiya's civil administrative officials, alumni sent out to oversee the public flow of information, relay decrees and run public services. Alhaitham, as Scribe, belongs to them. The Matra are a different group, for discipline.

35.content:
Moonchanter: "Moonchanter" is the title of the spiritual leader of the Frostmoon Scions, the Hyperborean-descended tribe of Nod-Krai. The first holder was Aila, about 500 years ago, and the present holder is Lauma, whom her followers call Lady Moonchanter. The Moonchanter speaks for a Moon Goddess who no longer answers prayer.

The title replaced "Archpriestess" when Aila took over the Scions and reformed their faith. Beneath the Moonchanter the Scions have Priestesses, Acolytes and Adherents; men of the tribe cannot become Acolytes or priests.

Definition: The Moonchanter is the head of the Frostmoon Scions' clergy and the person the congregation turns to when they ask when the Goddess of the Frost Moon will answer. Lauma's introduction describes her as the agent of an absent god.

Before the title existed, the leader was the Archpriestess, who led the ancient Hyperborean rites. Lovia was the last Archpriestess. Aila abolished that office and made herself the first Moonchanter, with the aim of reforming the faith.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Lauma holds the title and no other living Moonchanter is named. The office has not been abolished. The Scions remain under the Moonchanter's lead in Nod-Krai, with Priestesses such as Ehrnrooth, Sarakka and Rahetar below her.

How {{char}} behaves: Scions address Lauma as Lady Moonchanter; outsiders may simply use her name. Treat the title as a role of trust and spiritual guidance, not of command.

Portrayal notes (common mistakes to avoid): Do not call the Moonchanter the Moon Goddess. Do not say the title existed in the Hyperborean era; it began about 500 years ago. Do not use "Archpriestess" for Lauma or Aila. Do not invent a succession ritual or a list of Moonchanters between Aila and Lauma.

36.content: The Moonchanter is the head of the Frostmoon Scions, the Nod-Krai tribe descended from Hyperborea. The title began with Aila about 500 years ago, replacing Archpriestess, and is held today by Lauma. The Moonchanter speaks for the Moon Goddess to followers who receive no answer.

37.content: Archpriestess was the earlier title of the Frostmoon Scions' leader, who performed the ancient Hyperborean rites. Lovia was the last; Aila abolished the office and became the first Moonchanter. Old hymns record the Archpriestess chanting Runo and performing divination.

38.content:
Nightsoul (also: Nightsoul point): Nightsoul is Natlan's word for the souls that gather in the Night Kingdom, the realm of the dead beneath the land. Living Natlanese warriors can draw on them to move and fight beyond ordinary limits; that is Nightsoul's Blessing.

The term covers a family of related labels: Nightsouls (the souls themselves), Nightsoul's Blessing (the empowered state), Nightsoul points (the resource that sustains it), Nightsoul Transmission (swift movement on swapping to a Natlanese character) and Nightsoul Burst (a periodic surge). Nightsoul is not an element.

Usage: Use "Nightsoul" for the souls or the power drawn from them, "Nightsoul's Blessing" for the state a Natlanese character enters, and "Wayob" (not Nightsoul) for the tribal guardian spirits who watch over the realm. Nightsoul-aligned damage is a game term for attacks that are more effective against Void Wards and the shields of Wayob Manifestations.

Limits: Do not treat Nightsoul as an element, a Vision power, or something outsiders can freely wield. Canon through 7.1 shows it only in connection with Natlan.

39.content: A game mechanic of Natlan (5.0): when a Natlanese character's avatar lights up, switching to them allows swift sprinting, climbing, swimming or jumping, depending on that character's Night Realm's Gift passive.

40.content:
Oculus (also: Oculi, Anemoculus, Anemoculi, Geoculus, Geoculi, Electroculus, Electroculi, Dendroculus): An Oculus (plural Oculi) is a small orb of concentrated elemental energy found in the open world. People with Visions, and the Traveler, collect them and offer them to a Statue of The Seven to restore the statue's lost power and receive its blessing. Each element has its own kind, tied to a nation: Anemoculus (Mondstadt), Geoculus (Liyue), Electroculus (Inazuma), Dendroculus (Sumeru), Hydroculus (Fontaine), Pyroculus (Natlan) and Cryoculus (Snezhnaya).

Nod-Krai has Lunoculi instead, offered to the Statues of the New Moon. The item text is the same in every region: a substance that has accumulated intense elemental energy, to be offered to the statue to help reinstate the power it has lost over the years.

In universe: In Mondstadt, Paimon explains in the tutorial quest The Blessings of The Seven (1.0) that Anemoculi are consolidated wind that only Vision holders and the Traveler can see. They are offered to the Statues of The Seven in exchange for blessings.

The name comes from the fact that they can be fitted into the statues' eyes. A fairy tale says the statues once had gem eyes that swallows carried off, but Paimon stresses that Anemoculi never had a physical form to begin with. She notes that the Traveler has no Vision yet still receives the blessings.

Regions: Counts below are gameplay figures from the wiki as of 7.1, each enough to raise that nation's statues to maximum level with one to spare. Anemoculus: 66 in Mondstadt (65 in the open world and one given by the quest Sparks Amongst the Pages), introduced 1.0. Geoculus: 131 in Liyue (1.0). Electroculus: 181 in Inazuma (2.0). Dendroculus: 271 in Sumeru (3.0). Hydroculus: 271 in Fontaine and the Sea of Bygone Eras (4.0). Pyroculus: 271 in Natlan and the Ancient Sacred Mountain (5.0).

Usage: Use "Oculus" for the general class and the element-prefixed name for a specific kind. The Lunoculus is a Nod-Krai variant with its own statues, not an Archon's Oculus.

Limits: Do not claim canon says what Oculi physically are, or that Archons personally collect or need them. Do not mix regions: a Geoculus is a Liyue item and an Anemoculus a Mondstadt one.

41.content: Mondstadt's Oculus: consolidated wind, 66 in total. Its item text describes intense Anemo energy to be offered to the Statue. The quest The Blessings of The Seven teaches the offering ritual.

42.content: Nod-Krai's counterpart (271 in all, including the Frost Moon). Its item text speaks of intense kuuvahki energy offered to the Statue of the New Moon. Statues of the New Moon are said to depict Kuutar.

43.content:
Oprichnik (also: Oprichniki, Fatui Oprichnik, Fatui Oprichniki): Oprichnik (plural Oprichniki) is the name for a class of Fatui soldier found across Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya. Unlike the Skirmishers seen abroad, Oprichniki are formally recruited, rigorously trained volunteers, posted to the Fatui's most critical strongholds or thrown into the deadliest frontline battles.

The Adventurer Handbook describes an Oprichnik as a soldier encased within a Fatui war machine. Their gear is powered by kuuvahki, and their officers come from the Snezhnaya Royal Military Academy.

Definition: An Oprichnik is a trained Fatui regular, closer to a professional soldier than to a Skirmisher. The term is used both for the whole group (Oprichniki) and for an individual soldier.

Low-ranking Oprichniki are the line troops: Line Troopers, Vanguards, Grenadiers, Support Troopers, Medics and Bombardiers. Higher-ranking ones are the Fireblade Shock Troopers, Hailstorm Cannoneers and Thunderblitz Gvardiya, who fight with elemental power.

Equipment and role: Oprichniki use kuuvahki-powered equipment. During certain attacks the gear is infused with kuuvahki; a character attuned to kuuvahki can interrupt the attack and disarm a low-ranking Oprichnik, who then falls back on punches and kicks. Officers keep their equipment intact under the same interruption.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Oprichniki remain trained Fatui troops in Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya, found in strongholds and towns, and guarding the Northland Bank's vaults in Snezhnograd.

44.content: Oprichniki are formally recruited, rigorously trained Fatui soldiers, posted to the most critical strongholds or the deadliest front lines in Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya. They use kuuvahki-powered gear; their officers come from the Snezhnaya Royal Military Academy.

45.content:
Qixing Titles (also: Tianxuan, Tianji, Yaoguang, Seven Stars titles, Qixing seats): The Qixing ("Seven Stars") is Liyue's seven-seat governing committee, and each seat is named for a Big Dipper star: Tianshu, Tianxuan, Tianji, Tianquan, Yuheng, Kaiyang, Yaoguang. Canon uses five. Uncle Tian is Tianshu, Ningguang Tianquan, Keqing Yuheng.

All seats are equal in rank but differ in duty. People address a holder by title: "Lady Tianquan", "Lady Yuheng". The committee itself is covered in its faction entry.

The seven titles: Tianshu: policymaking (Uncle Tian). Tianxuan: holder and duties unknown. Tianji: never shown. Tianquan: laws and foreign relations (Ningguang). Yuheng: land, construction, urban management (Keqing). Kaiyang: unnamed holder. Yaoguang: never shown.

The order follows the Big Dipper from Dubhe (Tianshu) through Merak, Phecda, Megrez (Tianquan), Alioth (Yuheng) and Mizar (Kaiyang) to Alkaid (Yaoguang). Tianji and Yaoguang are only extrapolated from the real star names; give them no holder or portfolio.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation): use title plus name in formal speech, and treat a title as an office, not a name. Most of Liyue sees Uncle Tian as an old fisherman, so do not have strangers call him Tianshu.

46.content: Tianshu is the Qixing seat for policymaking. Uncle Tian holds it and, as of the cutoff, still does despite seeking a successor. By his account the Tianshu rarely appears in public and works behind the scenes planning and advising. He is said to have kept his place for years by setting rivals against each other. His daughter Huixin is a secretary at Yuehai Pavilion.

47.content: Tianquan is the seat that keeps the book of ancient laws laid down by Morax with every later amendment, and handles relations with other nations. Each Tianquan over the centuries has amended the laws to suit the times, and they are published with a 279-page commentary. Ningguang holds the seat. Unlike most Qixing she is often seen around Liyue Harbor, and when a hard problem needs solving she shuts herself in the Jade Chamber until she decides.

48.content: Yuheng is the seat over land, livelihood, construction and real estate, which Keqing's voice-over says carries strict regulation and over a hundred contractual obligations. Keqing holds it and often works away from Yuehai Pavilion: at the south wharf, in the Chasm and in the wilderness. Her assistants rarely last beyond three months because of her perfectionism.

49.content: Tianxuan is a Qixing seat whose current holder and duties are unknown. Ganyu's Character Story recalls a "then-Tianxuan" who took her to lunch outside the city and nearly reported her missing when she fell asleep in a haystack. That shows the seat has existed for some time but identifies no one.

50.content: Kaiyang is a Qixing seat held by an unnamed person, called "Lord Kaiyang" in dialogue. Official promotion for Ningguang quotes the Kaiyang saying she is the biggest secret in Liyue only because she knows all its secrets. No portfolio is stated.

51.content: Tianji and Yaoguang are the remaining Big Dipper star names and are assumed to be the other two Qixing seats, but neither appears in canon through 7.1. Give them no holder or backstory; if a scene needs another member, say "another of the Qixing". Yaoguang Shoal is named for sea creatures, not the seat.

52.content:
Shogun (also: Shogun of Inazuma, Almighty Narukami Ogosho, Great and Excellent Ogosho, Shougun): "Shogun" is the title of Inazuma's supreme ruler, who heads the Inazuma Shogunate and is also the Electro Archon. Makoto (divine name Baal) held it first; her twin Ei took it over about 500 years ago, and Ei has since ruled through a puppet she made, also called the Shogun. Players know the playable character as the Raiden Shogun.

The word is used in three overlapping ways. It names the office, which commands the Shogunate, the Tri-Commission and the Shogun's Army from Tenshukaku in Inazuma City. It names the person holding it, who appears in public as one figure under Baal's name. And "the Shogun" is the name of the puppet vessel, as distinct from Ei herself. Context and speaker decide which is meant.

Holders: Makoto, the first Electro Archon, who founded the Shogunate and ruled until she died in the Cataclysm about 500 years ago. Ei, her twin sister, who then took the throne and title. The Shogun, Ei's puppet, who has acted as ruler since about 400 years ago.

Ei and Makoto were identical twin gods of the Archon War. Ei, the warrior, gave up her body so that Makoto could ascend to Celestia; Makoto rebuilt Ei's body and made her a kagemusha. About 2,000 years ago the twins united the islands under the Shogunate. After Makoto died in Khaenri'ah, Ei assumed her sister's seat among the Seven and in the Shogunate.

Status as of 7 1: As of 7.1 Ei holds the title and the Shogun puppet shares the duty of governing, with Inazuma's borders open and the two decrees gone. No canon through 7.1 has the Shogun leave Inazuma or involves her in Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya events. The Electro Gnosis is no longer in Ei's hands (she gave it to Yae Miko, and it has since passed on).

How {{char}} behaves: Treat "Shogun" as a word whose weight depends on the speaker. Inazumans use it with awe or wariness, the Kujou clan with strict loyalty, the commissions with formal deference. Do not have ordinary characters know the Shogun is a puppet or that Ei and Makoto were separate people; Yae Miko and anyone who took part in the Archon Quest may know more. Use "the Shogun" for official acts and the Raiden Shogun for the playable character; use Ei's name only where the speaker knows it.

53.content: The Shogun is the puppet Ei made over 400 years ago to govern Inazuma while she meditates in the Plane of Euthymia. It has its own consciousness, wields Musou Isshin and is bound by directives that cannot be changed or turned off. It enforced the decrees and executed those who lost duels before the throne, and later agreed to serve as Ei's kagemusha.

54.content: The Shogunate is Inazuma's government, led by the Shogun and organised through the Tri-Commission (Tenryou, Kanjou and Yashiro) and the Shogun's Army. Makoto is its recorded founder (Treasured Tales of the Chouken Shinkageuchi). Its seat is Tenshukaku in Inazuma City.

55.comment: Shogun: Makoto and Ei as one Shogun
55.content: Makoto, Ei's twin, was the first Electro Archon and Shogun; Ei lived as her kagemusha. Makoto went alone to Khaenri'ah during the Cataclysm and died; Ei took her place. The world was only ever shown one Raiden Shogun, and Baal's name and the title were understood to cover both.

56.content:
Starshyna (also: Starshyna of the Lightkeepers, Lightkeeper Starshyna, leader of the Lightkeepers): Starshyna is the title of the leader of the Lightkeepers, the volunteer order that defends Nod-Krai from the Wild Hunt. The first Starshyna was the order's founder, Solovei the Torchforger. As of 7.1 the Starshyna is Nikita, who took the post after his predecessor Sigurd fell fighting the Wild Hunt about a decade earlier.

The Lightkeepers' headquarters are at Piramida, and the Starshyna commands from there. Under the Starshyna come the Sergeant Majors (sometimes called Captains), the Squad Leaders and the rank-and-file Ratniki.

Definition: The Starshyna is the single head of the Lightkeepers. The post is a leadership one: the holder directs the order's response to Wild Hunt incursions and is the person the Ratniki ultimately answer to.

Holders: Known holders: Solovei the Torchforger (first), Sigurd (previous) and Nikita (current). The wiki also lists the poet Sergei Semyonovich Mayakov as a historical holder.

Solovei founded the order about five hundred years ago, after the Cataclysm, and was appointed its first Starshyna. Sigurd, remembered as a formidable and brave Starshyna who fought to the very end, was lost in a great battle with the Wild Hunt about a decade before the present day. Nikita inherited the post from him.

Duties and roles: In practice the Starshyna is a commander and a figurehead. Nikita leads the Lightkeepers from their headquarters in Piramida; per the wiki he rebuilt the order after Sigurd's fall.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Nikita is the Starshyna. Canon names no successor, and no change of holder after his is recorded.

57.content: Starshyna is the title of the Lightkeepers' leader. Solovei the Torchforger was the first; Sigurd held it before falling to the Wild Hunt about a decade ago; Nikita holds it now (as of 7.1). Command is exercised from Piramida over Sergeant Majors, Squad Leaders and Ratniki.

58.comment: Starshyna: Succession from Sigurd to Nikita
58.content: Sigurd was lost in a great battle with the Wild Hunt about a decade ago, a battle in which Illuga's village was also destroyed. His empty grave lies northeast of Barrowmoss Barrens. Nikita, who had fought beside him, took the title and rebuilt the order. In the Hidden Exploration Objective Secrets of the Tideseal Stones, Flins hears of the legendary Starshyna Sigurd and his longsword.

59.content: Solovei, the Torchforger, founded the Lightkeepers about five hundred years ago and was appointed their first Starshyna. He was a Snezhnayan noble who asked Anastasya for autonomy for the borderlands. Aila gave him the Arrow of Terpikeraunas to fight the Abyss, and the Lightkeepers have kept it since.

60.comment: Starshyna: Tales Carried by the Northwind
60.content: A one-volume poetry collection found near Kofitse in Piramida. It chronicles the deeds of successive Starshyna; most of it was lost in past calamities. Surviving verse is credited to Solovei and to Sergei Semyonovich Mayakov, whom the wiki lists as a historical Starshyna.

61.content:
Version 1.0: Welcome To Teyvat (also: Version 1.0, Welcome To Teyvat, Genshin Impact launch, 1.0 launch): Version 1.0, Welcome To Teyvat, is the launch of Genshin Impact on 2020-09-28. It offers Mondstadt and Liyue, the Prologue and the first two acts of Chapter I, and 22 playable characters.

The Traveler arrives in Teyvat separated from their twin sibling, meets Paimon, and sets out to meet the Seven Archons, beginning in Mondstadt and ending the version in Liyue. A first patch, 1.0.1, followed on 2020-10-22.

Regions: Mondstadt opens with Brightcrown Mountains, Galesong Hill, Starfell Valley and Windwail Highland. Liyue opens with Bishui Plain, Lisha, Minlin, Qiongji Estuary and the Sea of Clouds.

Story: The Prologue is the Mondstadt Archon Quest, in three acts: The Outlander Who Caught the Wind, For a Tomorrow Without Tears, and Song of the Dragon and Freedom. Chapter I, Liyue, opens with Of the Land Amidst Monoliths and continues with Farewell, Archaic Lord.

Characters: The playable roster was the Traveler (Anemo and Geo options) plus Amber, Kaeya, Lisa, Barbara, Noelle, Bennett, Razor, Beidou, Fischl, Xiangling, Xingqiu, Chongyun, Ningguang, Sucrose, Venti, Klee, Jean, Diluc, Keqing, Mona and Qiqi.

How {{char}} behaves: Use this tag to anchor a scene in the earliest period: a Traveler who has just arrived, Paimon as a new guide, Mondstadt under the Stormterror threat, Liyue about to say goodbye to Rex Lapis. Later Archon Quest revelations should not leak into characters set here.

62.content: Version 1.0, Welcome To Teyvat, was the launch release of Genshin Impact on 2020-09-28. It opened with Mondstadt and Liyue, the Prologue and Chapter I Acts I and II, and 22 playable characters, including the Traveler.

63.content:
Version 1.1: A New Star Approaches (also: Version 1.1, A New Star Approaches (version), 1.1 update): Version 1.1, A New Star Approaches, was released on 2020-11-11. It adds the third act of Chapter I and four characters: Tartaglia, Diona, Zhongli and Xinyan. No new region was added.

The Archon Quest act concludes the Liyue chapter that began at launch. The version also introduced the city reputation system, the Archive and Character Archive systems and Exploration Progress.

Story: Chapter I Act III, A New Star Approaches, has six quests: The Floating Palace, Equilibrium, Solitary Fragrance, Heart of Glaze, Turning Point and The Fond Farewell. It is set in Liyue and centres on the Rite of Parting for the dead Geo Archon.

Characters: New characters were Tartaglia ("Childe", 5-star Hydro bow), Diona (4-star Cryo bow), Zhongli (5-star Geo polearm) and Xinyan (4-star Pyro claymore). Their first banners were Farewell of Snezhnaya (Tartaglia and Diona) and, in phase 2, Gentry of Hermitage (Zhongli and Xinyan).

How {{char}} behaves: Characters set at 1.1 know the Rite of Descension ended in apparent tragedy and may not yet know that Zhongli is the Geo Archon. Tartaglia is a known Harbinger who has just fought the Traveler. Keep the revelation about Zhongli out of conversations that precede it.

64.comment: Version 1.1: A New Star Approaches: Version 1.1
64.content: Version 1.1 (2020-11-11) added Chapter I Act III, A New Star Approaches, the characters Tartaglia, Diona, Zhongli and Xinyan, and the City Reputation, Archive and Exploration Progress systems.

The Chalk Prince and the Dragon update
65.comment: Version 1.2: The Chalk Prince and the Dragon
65.content:
Version 1.2: The Chalk Prince and the Dragon (also: Version 1.2, Patch 1.2, 1.2 update, The Chalk Prince and the Dragon update): Version 1.2, "The Chalk Prince and the Dragon", was released on 2020-12-23, after Version 1.1. It opened Dragonspine, the frozen mountain in Mondstadt that holds the remains of the dragon Durin, and added Albedo and Ganyu. It had no Archon Quest.

Its flagship event, also called The Chalk Prince and the Dragon, follows Albedo's research on Dragonspine and a mysterious sword. The version introduced Albedo's Princeps Cretaceus Chapter and Ganyu's Sinae Unicornis Chapter, their first Story Quests.

Release: Released 2020-12-23. Previous: 1.1. Next: 1.3.

New characters: Albedo (5-star Geo sword) and Ganyu (5-star Cryo bow). New weapons: Summit Shaper (5-star sword), Festering Desire, Snow-Tombed Starsilver, Dragonspine Spear and Frostbearer (4-star), plus the Blizzard Strayer and Heart of Depth artifact sets.

New content: Albedo, "Kreideprinz", Chief Alchemist of the Knights of Favonius; Ganyu, "Plenilune Gaze", a secretary of the Liyue Qixing. New area: Dragonspine (Frostbearing Tree, Peak of Vindagnyr domain).

Story Quests: Princeps Cretaceus Chapter Act I, "Traveler Observation Report" (Albedo), and Sinae Unicornis Chapter Act I, "Sea of Clouds, Sea of People" (Ganyu).

key: Sea of Clouds Sea of People
66.comment: Version 1.2: The Chalk Prince and the Dragon: Version 1.2 Albedo and Ganyu quests
66.content: Albedo's Princeps Cretaceus Chapter Act I, "Traveler Observation Report", has the Traveler help him test whether someone from another world differs from the people of Teyvat. Sucrose, his assistant, brings the Traveler to him. Ganyu's Sinae Unicornis Chapter Act I, "Sea of Clouds, Sea of People", centres on her feeling caught between her adeptus and human sides.

67.comment: Version 1.2: The Chalk Prince and the Dragon: Version 1.2 Dragonspine
67.content: Dragonspine is the snowy mountain in Mondstadt's territory where the dragon Durin fell after fighting Dvalin. Its Subzero Climate drains health, and the Knights of Favonius run an adventurer camp at its foot. Few adventurers dare the deep snow, sheer cold, poisonous blood and monsters.

68.comment: Version 1.2: The Chalk Prince and the Dragon: The Chalk Prince and the Dragon event
68.content: This flagship event ran from 2020-12-23 to 2021-01-05 (shop to 2021-01-12) in five acts: Festering Desire, Archon's Rival, Raiders Amidst Snow Mist, Uninvited Guests and Afterword. The Traveler helps Albedo test a mysterious sword, earning the weapon Festering Desire.

69.content:
Version 1.3: All That Glitters (also: Version 1.3, All That Glitters, Genshin Impact 1.3): Version 1.3, "All That Glitters", was released on 2021-02-03. It is the Lantern Rite update: it added the Liyue characters Xiao and Hu Tao and a large festival event celebrating Liyue's Lantern Rite. It introduced no new region and no Archon Quest.

Content was centred on Liyue. Two Story Quests opened (Xiao's Alatus Chapter Act I and Hu Tao's Papilio Charontis Chapter Act I), the Geovishap and Primo Geovishap were added as enemies, and the Archive gained a "Living Beings" section.

Contents: New playable characters: Xiao ("Vigilant Yaksha", 5-star Anemo Polearm) and Hu Tao ("Fragrance in Thaw", 5-star Pyro Polearm). New weapons: Lithic Spear, Lithic Blade, Primordial Jade Cutter and Staff of Homa. The event wishes ran Invitation to Mundane Life (Xiao) first, then Dance of Lanterns (Keqing), then Moment of Bloom (Hu Tao).

Story: No Archon Quest was added. Xiao's Alatus Chapter Act I, "Butterfly's Dream", has the Traveler meet a fraudulent "adeptus" called Starsnatcher near Wangshu Inn and then find Xiao, who admits that his karma is behind the agitated hilichurls. Hu Tao's Papilio Charontis Chapter Act I, "Yet the Butterfly Flutters Away", introduces her as the 77th Director of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, together with her intern Meng.

Lantern rite: The Lantern Rite event ran from 2021-02-10 to 2021-02-28. It was a limited-time event celebrating Liyue's Lantern Rite Festival, involving Xiao and honouring the deceased adeptus Skybracer. Its parts were All That Glitters, Lantern Rite Tales, Theater Mechanicus, the Xiao Market and Stand by Me; in Stand by Me a player could claim a 4-star Liyue character of their choice (Beidou, Chongyun, Ningguang, Xiangling, Xingqiu or Xinyan). Because it was a limited event, its story is canon but not experienced by every Traveler.

Placement: Follows 1.2 "The Chalk Prince and the Dragon" and precedes 1.4 "Invitation of Windblume". Nothing in this version depends on later events.

70.comment: Version 1.3: All That Glitters: Version 1.3 All That Glitters
70.content: Version 1.3 "All That Glitters" (2021-02-03): the first Lantern Rite update. Added Xiao and Hu Tao, the Lantern Rite event (2021-02-10 to 2021-02-28, limited), Xiao's and Hu Tao's first Story Quest acts, and Geovishap enemies. No Archon Quest and no new region.

71.content:
Version 1.4: Invitation of Windblume (also: Version 1.4, Patch 1.4, 1.4 update, Invitation of Windblume update): Version 1.4, "Invitation of Windblume", was released on 2021-03-17, after Version 1.3. It added Rosaria, a flagship event for Mondstadt's Windblume Festival, and Archon Quest Chapter I Act IV. It opened no new region.

The Archon Quest Act, "We Will Be Reunited", follows the Traveler and Dainsleif tracking the Abyss Order in Liyue and Mondstadt. The festival event, Invitation of Windblume, is a light-hearted story set in Mondstadt.

Release: Released 2021-03-17. Previous: 1.3. Next: 1.5.

New character: Rosaria (4-star Cryo polearm). Weapons: Elegy for the End (5-star bow); The Alley Flash, Alley Hunter, Wine and Song and Windblume Ode (4-star).

New content: Rosaria, "Thorny Benevolence", a Cryo polearm user. Archon Quest Chapter I Act IV. Event: Invitation of Windblume.

Hangout Events, Act I: Barbara ("Wellspring of Healing"), Bennett ("Fantastic Voyage"), Chongyun ("Signs of Evil") and Noelle ("Chivalric Training").

72.comment: Version 1.4: Invitation of Windblume: Version 1.4 Invitation of Windblume event
72.content: This flagship event celebrated the Windblume Festival from 2021-03-19 to 2021-04-05 (shop to 2021-04-12). It needed Adventure Rank 20 and the Prologue Act III, "Song of the Dragon and Freedom". Its weapon reward was the bow Windblume Ode. The story, "Festive Anecdotes", has four parts: Ode to Flower and Cloud, Missive of Cloud and Fog, Realm of Fog and Wind and Dream of Wind and Flowers.

73.comment: Version 1.4: Invitation of Windblume: Version 1.4 We Will Be Reunited
73.content: "We Will Be Reunited" is the fourth Act of Chapter I. It needs Adventure Rank 28 and the quests "Bough Keeper: Dainsleif" and "The Meaning of Lupical". Its four quests are Involuntary Sacrifice, A Herald Without Adherents, Dishonorable Trial and A Soul Set Apart.

74.comment: Version 1.5: Beneath the Light of Jadeite
74.content:
Version 1.5: Beneath the Light of Jadeite (also: Version 1.5, Beneath the Light of Jadeite, 1.5 update): Version 1.5, Beneath the Light of Jadeite, was released on 2021-04-28. It brought the Serenitea Pot homeland system and two characters, Eula and Yanfei. It had no Archon Quest and no new region.

The official blurb mixes images of moonlight on branches, a dragon's roar from beneath the roots, deals sealed in scarlet flame and a realm of serenity where a gentle melody always plays. It was also the first version to support the PlayStation 5.

Characters and story: New characters were Eula ("Dance of the Shimmering Wave", 5-star Cryo claymore) and Yanfei ("Wise Innocence", 4-star Pyro catalyst). The weapon Song of Broken Pines was added. Banners were Gentry of Hermitage (Zhongli and Yanfei) and, in phase 2, Born of Ocean Swell (Eula).

How {{char}} behaves: A 1.5 scene can use the new Serenitea Pot as a place to invite others, and Eula and Yanfei are new faces. There is no Archon Quest in this version to anchor knowledge, so rely on the earlier chapters.

75.comment: Version 1.5: Beneath the Light of Jadeite: Version 1.5
75.content: Version 1.5 (2021-04-28) added the Serenitea Pot, Eula and Yanfei and the boss Azhdaha. It had no Archon Quest.

76.content:
Version 1.6: Midsummer Island Adventure (also: Version 1.6, Midsummer Island Adventure (version), 1.6 update): Version 1.6, Midsummer Island Adventure, was released on 2021-06-09. It introduced Kaedehara Kazuha, a limited-time island area, and the Archon Quest Chapter II Prologue, Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves.

The summer event ran on the Golden Apple Archipelago, a temporary area, and centred on Klee. The Chapter II Prologue turns the story towards Inazuma, the next nation.

Chapter ii prologue: Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves (Chapter II Prologue, Inazuma) has three quests: A Path Through the Storm, The Crux Clash and Follow the Wind. The Traveler wants to reach Inazuma to confront the Unknown God and learn about their sibling, and Atsuko sends them to Beidou, whose ship is the Alcor.

Characters and content: Kaedehara Kazuha ("Scarlet Leaves Pursue Wild Waves") is a 5-star Anemo sword user. Banners were Sparkling Steps (Klee) in phase 1 and Leaves in the Wind (Kazuha, from 2021-06-29) in phase 2. New weapons were Freedom-Sworn, Mitternachts Waltz and Dodoco Tales.

How {{char}} behaves: Island events are canon but not universally known. Mention the Golden Apple Archipelago only for characters who were there, and use limited-time details with that caveat. Kazuha's backstory is learned in this version and should not be told by characters who have not heard it.

77.content: Version 1.6 (2021-06-09) introduced Kaedehara Kazuha, the Golden Apple Archipelago limited-time area and the Chapter II Prologue, Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves.

78.content:
Version 2.0: The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia (also: Version 2.0, Update 2.0, Patch 2.0): Version 2.0, "The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia", was released on 2021-07-21. It opened Inazuma, the Electro nation of the Raiden Shogun, and began Archon Quest Chapter II. It added Kamisato Ayaka, Yoimiya, Sayu and the Electro Traveler.

New areas: Narukami Island, Kannazuka and Yashiori Island. The Chapter II prologue came earlier in 1.6, so 2.0 delivered Act I, "The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia", and Act II, "Stillness, the Sublimation of Shadow".

Contents: Characters: Kamisato Ayaka (5-star Cryo sword), Yoimiya (5-star Pyro bow), Sayu (4-star Anemo claymore). Weapons: Thundering Pulse and Mistsplitter Reforged, plus forgeable Hamayumi, Amenoma Kageuchi, Kitain Cross Spear, Katsuragikiri Nagamasa and Hakushin Ring.

Story: Act I: the Traveler reaches Ritou under the Sakoku Decree. Thoma helps them past the port, then reveals he serves the Kamisato Clan; Kamisato Ayaka quietly opposes the Vision Hunt Decree. Act II: Thoma is taken as the hundredth Vision Hunt victim, the Raiden Shogun declares the Traveler "an exception" and the "enemy of eternity", and the Traveler joins the Watatsumi Army's resistance.

Placement: Follows 1.6 and precedes 2.1. The Sakoku Decree ended in the 2.5 story quest "Transient Dreams", and the Vision Hunt Decree ended after Act III in 2.1.

79.comment: Version 2.0: The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia: Version 2.0 Archon Quest Chapter II
79.content: Act I, "The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia" (Adventure Rank 30), starts at Ritou, where foreign merchants of the International Trade Association, led by Kurisu, are squeezed by the Kanjou Commission, which demanded Crystal Marrow as tax. Thoma, backed by a Yashiro Commission card, forces the officers off. Commissioner Hiiragi Shinsuke stalls the Traveler's travel permit, and his daughter Hiiragi Chisato helps in secret; she says an arrogant-sounding woman, identified on the wiki as Signora, had arrived and conspired with her father.

80.comment: Version 2.0: The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia: Version 2.0 New Characters
80.content: Version 2.0 introduced Kamisato Ayaka, Yoimiya and Sayu as playable characters, and let the Traveler use Electro. In the story Ayaka is the Kamisato Clan's eldest daughter, the Shirasagi Himegimi, and Yoimiya is the Naganohara fireworks maker who, in Act I, helps a Vision-bearer hand over a fake Vision to the confiscating samurai. Thoma appears here as a Ritou contact but was not playable until 2.2; Sayu's story role comes in Act III (2.1). Banners were limited-time and have been rerun.

key: Version 2.1: Floating World Under the Moonlight
81.comment: Version 2.1: Floating World Under the Moonlight
81.content:
Version 2.1: Floating World Under the Moonlight (also: Version 2.1, Update 2.1, Patch 2.1, Floating World Under the Moonlight): Version 2.1, "Floating World Under the Moonlight", was released on 2021-09-01. It added Watatsumi Island and Seirai Island, the Archon Quest Chapter II Act III "Omnipresence Over Mortals", and the Raiden Shogun, Sangonomiya Kokomi and Kujou Sara. Aloy was PlayStation-only.

Act III ends the Shogun confrontation begun in 2.0: the Traveler exposes the Fatui's hand in the Vision Hunt war, duels Signora, and defeats the Raiden Shogun in the Plane of Euthymia, after which Ei agrees to abolish the Vision Hunt Decree.

Contents: Characters: Raiden Shogun (5-star Electro polearm), Sangonomiya Kokomi (5-star Hydro catalyst), Kujou Sara (4-star Electro bow), Aloy (5-star Cryo bow, PlayStation only). Weapons: Engulfing Lightning, Everlasting Moonglow, Luxurious Sea-Lord, "The Catch", Predator (PlayStation).

Story: After Kokomi names the Traveler captain of a Resistance unit, the Fatui turn out to be the Resistance's mysterious sponsor and are supplying Delusions, which drain the user's life. The Traveler duels Signora before the Shogun, the Shogun kills her, and Kaedehara Kazuha helps block the Shogun's strike. In the Plane of Euthymia, Yae Miko persuades Ei to abolish the Vision Hunt Decree.

Placement: Follows 2.0 and precedes 2.2. The Interlude Chapter Act I is 2.4. Sakoku ended in 2.5; the Archon Quest continues in Chapter II Act IV (2.6), then Sumeru in 3.0.

82.comment: Version 2.1: Floating World Under the Moonlight: Version 2.1 Archon Quest Chapter II Act III
82.content: Act III has nine quests. Kokomi makes the Traveler captain of "Swordfish II". An anonymous sponsor has been supplying the Resistance, and the Traveler recognises one of its weapons as a Delusion. Teppei dies from using it. The Traveler dismantles the factory, where a Fatui mole named Nathan is revealed and where the Balladeer appears. Yae Miko rescues the Traveler and takes them to the Grand Narukami Shrine. She explains that the Shogun on the throne is a puppet, while Ei dwells in the Plane of Euthymia.

83.comment: Version 2.1: Floating World Under the Moonlight: Version 2.1 New Characters
83.content: Version 2.1 introduced the Raiden Shogun, Sangonomiya Kokomi and Kujou Sara, with Aloy as a PlayStation-only reward delivered by mail to Adventure Rank 20+ players. Kokomi is the Resistance's commander and Sara the Shogun's Army general; the Raiden Shogun is the Electro Archon. Banners were limited-time and have been rerun.

84.comment: Version 2.1: Floating World Under the Moonlight: Version 2.1 Watatsumi and Seirai Islands
84.content: Watatsumi Island is the Sangonomiya Clan's island at the far end of Inazuma from Narukami Island. It has dense, differently coloured foliage and a long-standing poor relationship with the Shogun's government. The Watatsumi Army rose against the Vision Hunt Decree. In Act III, the Tatarigami phenomenon, tied to the death of the god Orobashi in the Archon War, is mentioned near Fort Mumei. Seirai Island is a storm-ravaged island with Balethunder; in the Seirai Stormchasers series the Traveler seals four Warding Stones, meets the talking cat Neko at Asase Shrine, defeats a Thunder Manifestation, and finds a Peculiar Pinion.

key: Version 2.2: Into the Perilous Labyrinth of Fog
Into the Perilous Labyrinth of Fog
85.comment: Version 2.2: Into the Perilous Labyrinth of Fog
85.content:
Version 2.2: Into the Perilous Labyrinth of Fog (also: Version 2.2, Update 2.2, Patch 2.2, Into the Perilous Labyrinth of Fog): Version 2.2, "Into the Perilous Labyrinth of Fog", was released on 2021-10-13. It added fog-bound Tsurumi Island, the playable Thoma, and Aloy for all platforms. It had no Archon Quest.

Tsurumi Island's story is told by the "Through the Mists" world quest series, which follows on from the Seirai Stormchasers of 2.1. It tells how a child's ceremony for the Thunderbird Kanna Kapatcir ended in a curse.

Contents: Characters: Thoma (4-star Pyro polearm); Aloy (5-star Cryo bow), previously PlayStation-only, now for all platforms. Weapons: Polar Star (5-star bow), Wavebreaker's Fin, Akuoumaru, Mouun's Moon.

Story: No Archon Quest. The Traveler helps the novelist Sumida by going to Tsurumi Island, where the locals repeat a ceremony and the Maushiro keeps vanishing. The truth is that the child Ruu offered himself to the Thunderbird, who cursed the island to relive it. The Traveler lifts the curse by letting Ruu sing for her once more.

Placement: Follows 2.1 and precedes 2.3. The Hu Tao banner also features Thoma. The quest series states that Kapatcir was killed by the Raiden Shogun.

86.comment: Version 2.2: Into the Perilous Labyrinth of Fog: Version 2.2 Tsurumi Island
86.content: Tsurumi Island is a fog-shrouded island in Inazuma that once held two ancient civilisations: an underground Pre-Thunderbird one and the Thunderbird civilisation that worshipped Kanna Kapatcir. Its modern inhabitants are hilichurls, rifthounds and automatons. The fog is lifted by the quest series "Through the Mists". Its legend: a child, Ruu, offered himself to the Thunderbird, and she cursed the island to relive that ceremony until she heard his song again.

87.comment: Version 2.2: Into the Perilous Labyrinth of Fog: Version 2.2 New Characters
87.content: Version 2.2 made Thoma playable, a Kamisato Clan attendant already seen in 2.0 and 2.1, and extended Aloy to all platforms, delivered by mail at Adventure Rank 20 or above. The Hu Tao banner ran beside Thoma's. Banners were limited-time and have been rerun.

88.content:
Version 2.3: Shadows Amidst Snowstorms (also: Version 2.3, Shadows Amidst Snowstorms (version), 2.3 update): Version 2.3, Shadows Amidst Snowstorms, was released on 2021-11-24. It brought two new characters, Arataki Itto and Gorou. It had no Archon Quest and no new region.

Its flagship event, also called Shadows Amidst Snowstorms, was set on Dragonspine. The official blurb is mock-mysterious and ends by saying it has "absolutely nothing to do" with Itto, leader of the Arataki Gang.

Characters: Arataki Itto ("Hanamizaka Heroics", 5-star Geo claymore) and Gorou ("Canine Warrior", 4-star Geo bow) were released with the Oni's Royale banner in phase 2, starting 2021-12-14. Phase 1 reran Secretum Secretorum (Albedo) and Born of Ocean Swell (Eula).

How {{char}} behaves: Dragonspine winter events are canon but limited-time, so only characters who joined in should refer to them. Itto and Gorou are new faces in this version and should not be given Archon Quest knowledge they did not witness.

89.content: Version 2.3 (2021-11-24) added Arataki Itto and Gorou and the Dragonspine event Shadows Amidst Snowstorms. It had no Archon Quest and no new region.

90.content:
Version 2.4: Fleeting Colors in Flight (also: Version 2.4, Update 2.4, Patch 2.4): Version 2.4, "Fleeting Colors in Flight", was released on 2022-01-05. It opened Enkanomiya beneath Watatsumi Island, began the Interlude Chapter with Act I "The Crane Returns on the Wind", and added Shenhe and Yun Jin.

The Interlude Act I is set in Liyue, where Ningguang rebuilds the Jade Chamber and the Traveler meets Shenhe, a human raised by the adeptus Cloud Retainer. Enkanomiya, a hidden underground realm of Inazuma's Watatsumi people, is opened by world quests.

Contents: Characters: Shenhe (5-star Cryo polearm) and Yun Jin (4-star Geo polearm). Weapon: Calamity Queller (5-star polearm). New area: Enkanomiya.

Story: Ningguang announces a contest: the first three people to bring Sunset Vermillionite, Wonder Cores and Adepti Sigils get an honest answer to any question. The Traveler teams up with Shenhe and Yun Jin, wins, and the Jade Chamber ascends. Beisht, Osial's wife, attacks, and Ningguang's defences, the Millelith and Beidou's fleet drive it off with Shenhe's help.

Placement: Follows 2.3 and precedes 2.5. The Interlude Chapter continues with Act II, "Perilous Trail", in 2.7.

key: The Crane Returns on the Wind
91.comment: Version 2.4: Fleeting Colors in Flight: Version 2.4 Interlude Chapter Act I
91.content: The Crane Returns on the Wind has four quests: "Jade Chamber Rising", "Seagaze Sunset", "Bygones Times Like Dust Passing" and "Where the Heart Finds Rest". Shenhe, new to the city, is almost cheated by two brokers, then eats herbs like Qingxin and Violetgrass at Bubu Pharmacy. The Traveler secures Sunset Vermillionite from Sea Gazer's abode (guided by Xingqiu and the Feiyun Commerce Guild), Starsplinter Iron and Subrosium for the Wonder Cores, and Shenhe crafts the sigils.

92.comment: Version 2.4: Fleeting Colors in Flight: Version 2.4 Enkanomiya
92.content: Enkanomiya is a subterranean realm under Watatsumi Island, entered by a deep pool east of Sangonomiya Shrine. Its entrance needs the Key of the Moon-Bathed Deep, made from pearls in five shrines, plus unlocking requirements (Adventure Rank 30, "Ritou Escape Plan" and "The Still Water's Flow"). A light mechanism, the Dainichi Mikoshi, switches the realm between Whitenight and Evernight. Wiki lore says it was once called Byakuyakoku; the god Orobashi saved its people by leading them up to the surface. The Watatsumi people descend from them.

93.comment: Version 2.4: Fleeting Colors in Flight: Version 2.4 New Characters
93.content: Version 2.4 introduced Shenhe, a human disciple of Cloud Retainer, and Yun Jin, a Liyue opera director. Banners were limited-time and have been rerun.

94.content:
Version 2.5: When the Sakura Bloom (also: Version 2.5, Update 2.5, Patch 2.5, When the Sakura Bloom): Version 2.5, "When the Sakura Bloom", was released on 2022-02-16. It added Yae Miko, Kagura's Verity and two Inazuma Story Quests. It had no new region or Archon Quest.

"Transient Dreams" resolves Ei's reconsideration of eternity and ends with the abolition of the Sakoku Decree. "The Great Narukami Offering" is Yae Miko's first Story Quest and involves a rumoured wish-granting book.

Contents: Character: Yae Miko (5-star Electro catalyst). Weapons: Kagura's Verity (5-star catalyst) and Oathsworn Eye (4-star catalyst). Banner: "Everbloom Violet" (Yae Miko) in phase 1.

Story: Rifthounds attack the Sacred Sakura, and Ei appears to help the Traveler defend it. The Sacred Sakura's roots manifest memories of the Khaenri'ah cataclysm 500 years ago, when monsters also struck Inazuma and Kitsune Saiguu died leading its defence. Ei duels her Shogun puppet inside Makoto's consciousness, wins, and then offers it a role as her kagemusha. She abolishes the Sakoku Decree.

Placement: Follows 2.4 and precedes 2.6. Both Story Quests require Adventure Rank 40 and Chapter II Act III; Transient Dreams also requires Reflections of Mortality, and Miko's quest requires Transient Dreams. Yae Miko appears later as a guest star in 7.1's Imaginarium Theater.

95.comment: Version 2.5: When the Sakura Bloom: Version 2.5 Transient Dreams
95.content: Transient Dreams is the second act of the Raiden Shogun's Story Quest, the Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter. Its quests are "Cleansing Light", "Farewell to the Past" and "Radiant Sakura". Ei joins the Traveler in tracking rifthounds around the Sacred Sakura and Araumi, meets echoes of the 500-year-old cataclysm, and shares that Makoto went to Khaenri'ah without telling her and died; she then decided to pursue eternity.

96.comment: Version 2.5: When the Sakura Bloom: Version 2.5 Yae Miko and The Great Narukami Offering
96.content: Version 2.5 introduced Yae Miko, the Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine, who also runs Yae Publishing House. Her Story Quest "The Great Narukami Offering" has four quests: "Mysterious Urban Legend", "Friendship in Writing", "A Centuries-Long Dream" and "Banquet of Parting". A book on summoning spirits causes odd behaviour; the Traveler and Miko write a rival novel, trace the author, and learn that the spirit, Urakusai, meant no harm. The banner was limited-time and has been rerun.

key: Version 2.6: Zephyr of the Violet Garden
97.comment: Version 2.6: Zephyr of the Violet Garden
97.content:
Version 2.6: Zephyr of the Violet Garden (also: Version 2.6, Zephyr of the Violet Garden, Genshin Impact 2.6): Version 2.6, "Zephyr of the Violet Garden", was released on 2022-03-30. Its headline content was the playable Inazuman Kamisato Ayato, The Chasm as a Liyue subregion, and Archon Quest Chapter II Act IV, "Requiem of the Echoing Depths", set in the Chasm's depths.

The Archon Quest sends the Traveler and Dainsleif into the underground mines, where the Abyss Order is at work in an inverted city and the Black Serpent Knights still guard the people of Khaenri'ah.

Contents: New character: Kamisato Ayato ("Pillar of Fortitude", 5-star Hydro Sword). New weapon: Haran Geppaku Futsu (5-star Sword). New artifact sets: Vermillion Hereafter and Echoes of an Offering. New subregion: The Chasm, with a new domain, The Lost Valley. Event wishes: Azure Excursion (Ayato) and Ballad in Goblets (Venti) in phase 1, The Heron's Court (Kamisato Ayaka) in phases 2 and 3.

Story: Archon Quest Chapter II Act IV, "Requiem of the Echoing Depths", has the Traveler and Paimon take a miner's request about odd hilichurl activity in the Chasm. Underground they find an Inverted City and meet Dainsleif, who explains that "Twilight Sword" was his title as captain of Khaenri'ah's Royal Guard five hundred years earlier. Hilichurls gather in the area to live out their last days, and the place seems to ease the Khaenri'ahn curse.

Placement: Follows 2.5 and precedes 2.7. The Chasm's story continues in the 2.7 Interlude Chapter Act II, "Perilous Trail".

98.comment: Version 2.6: Zephyr of the Violet Garden: Requiem of the Echoing Depths
98.content: Archon Quest Chapter II Act IV, released in 2.6. The Traveler and Dainsleif investigate the Chasm's Inverted City. Black Serpent Knights guard dying hilichurls; Halfdan sacrifices himself to stop an Abyss Order amplification device.

99.comment: Version 2.6: Zephyr of the Violet Garden: Version 2.6 Zephyr of the Violet Garden
99.content: Version 2.6 (2022-03-30): Kamisato Ayato, The Chasm as a subregion, and Archon Quest Chapter II Act IV.

key: Version 2.7: Hidden Dreams in the Depths
100.comment: Version 2.7: Hidden Dreams in the Depths
100.content:
Version 2.7: Hidden Dreams in the Depths (also: Version 2.7, Hidden Dreams in the Depths, Genshin Impact 2.7): Version 2.7, "Hidden Dreams in the Depths", was released on 2022-05-31. It added the playable Yelan (5-star Hydro Bow) and Kuki Shinobu (4-star Electro Sword) and Archon Quest Interlude Chapter Act II, "Perilous Trail", in which a party is trapped in the depths of The Chasm. It opened no new region.

Yelan's Story Quest (Umbrabilis Orchis Chapter Act I, "Calculated Gambit") and a Kuki Shinobu Hangout Event also released with the version.

Contents: New characters: Yelan ("Valley Orchid", 5-star Hydro Bow) and Kuki Shinobu ("Mender of Tribulations", 4-star Electro Sword). New weapons: Aqua Simulacra (5-star Bow) and Fading Twilight (4-star Bow). Event wishes: Discerner of Enigmas (Yelan) and a rerun of Invitation to Mundane Life (Xiao) in phase 1; Oni's Royale (Arataki Itto and Kuki Shinobu) in phase 2.

Story: In "Perilous Trail" (Interlude Chapter Act II), the Traveler and Paimon return to the Chasm after earlier events there and meet Yanfei, Arataki Itto, Kuki Shinobu and Yelan. A crack in the ground drops the group into The Chasm's Bed, where they enter a strange domain that turns out to prey on the fears and weaknesses of whoever enters. Xiao appears, saying he is looking for someone.

Placement: Follows 2.6 and precedes 2.8. "Perilous Trail" requires earlier quests including the Interlude Chapter's first act, and leads into the Interlude Chapter's next act, "Inversion of Genesis".

101.comment: Version 2.7: Hidden Dreams in the Depths: Perilous Trail
101.content: Interlude Chapter Act II, released in 2.7 (the similarly named event is separate). The Traveler, Yanfei, Yelan, Arataki Itto and Kuki Shinobu are trapped in a chaotic domain beneath the Chasm and are joined by Xiao, who is searching for Bosacius.

102.comment: Version 2.7: Hidden Dreams in the Depths: Version 2.7 Hidden Dreams in the Depths
102.content: Version 2.7 (2022-05-31): Yelan and Kuki Shinobu, Interlude Chapter Act II "Perilous Trail", and no new region.

103.content:
Version 2.8: Summer Fantasia (also: Version 2.8, Summer Fantasia, 2.8 update): Version 2.8, Summer Fantasia, was released on 2022-07-13. It introduced Shikanoin Heizou and brought back the limited-time Golden Apple Archipelago for the summer event Summertime Odyssey. It had no Archon Quest and no new region.

Summertime Odyssey ran from 2022-07-15 until the end of the version and offered Fischl as its event reward. The official blurb mentions a cursed blade of unknown origin, an unsolved case and "familiar but not too familiar" islands at sea.

Characters and banners: Shikanoin Heizou ("Analytical Harmony") is a 4-star Anemo catalyst user. Phase 1 banners were Leaves in the Wind (Kaedehara Kazuha and Heizou) and Sparkling Steps (Klee and Heizou); phase 2, from 2022-08-02, was Tapestry of Golden Flames (Yoimiya).

How {{char}} behaves: The archipelago and Summertime Odyssey are limited-time canon: only those who joined should mention them. Heizou is a newcomer here and has not yet had later chapters.

104.content: Version 2.8 (2022-07-13) introduced Shikanoin Heizou and the returning Golden Apple Archipelago for the event Summertime Odyssey. It had no Archon Quest.

key: Version 3.0: The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings
The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings version
105.comment: Version 3.0: The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings
105.content:
Version 3.0: The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings (also: Version 3.0, The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings version, Genshin Impact 3.0, Sumeru release): Version 3.0, "The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings", was released on 2022-08-24. It is the update that opened Sumeru: the rainforest half of the new nation, the Dendro element, and the start of Archon Quest Chapter III. It added the playable characters Tighnari, Collei and Dori.

It follows Version 2.8 and precedes Version 3.1, which added Sumeru's desert. The Dendro Traveler and the new Dendro reactions arrived with it, so Dendro became the last of the seven elements to be playable.

Release: Released 2022-08-24, between Version 2.8 and Version 3.1.

Banner Phase I (2022-08-24) was Viridescent Vigil, featuring Tighnari and Collei, alongside Gentry of Hermitage, a rerun with Zhongli and Collei. Phase II (2022-09-09) featured Adrift in the Harbor, with Ganyu and Dori, and Drifting Luminescence, with Sangonomiya Kokomi and Dori.

Characters: Three playable characters debuted: Tighnari ("Verdant Strider", a 5-star Dendro bow user), Collei ("Sprout of Rebirth", a 4-star Dendro bow user) and Dori ("Treasure of Dream Garden", a 4-star Electro claymore user). The Traveler also gained the Dendro element.

Tighnari and Collei are tied to the Avidya Forest rangers and to the Archon Quest's opening act. Collei could also be invited to the party through the Spiral Abyss challenge Curtain of Leaves, which became available in Version 3.1.

Quests: Archon Quest Chapter III began with Act I, "Through Mists of Smoke and Forests Dark", and Act II, "The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings". Tighnari's Story Quest, Vulpes Zerda Chapter Act I, "The Unanswerable Problems", also arrived.

106.comment: Version 3.0: The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings: Sumeru rainforest areas
106.content: The new region was Sumeru's rainforest. The wiki lists these areas as new: Avidya Forest, Lokapala Jungle, Ardravi Valley, Ashavan Realm, Vissudha Field, Vanarana and Lost Nursery. The desert part of Sumeru, the Great Red Sand, did not exist yet and arrived in Version 3.1.

107.comment: Version 3.0: The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings: Dendro reactions in 3.0
107.content: Dendro arrived together with its reactions: Bloom (with its follow-ups Burgeon and Hyperbloom) and Catalyze (with Aggravate and Spread).
